signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records JPY as the weekly leader at +0.792% across 7 pairs while AUD lags at −0.792% across 4 pairs, generating an extreme 1.584% leader-to-laggard bilateral spread. This strength occurs despite an acute carry deficit, with RBA at 4.85% vs BoJ at 1.25% yielding a 360bp policy rate spread and an overnight AONIA-TONA differential of +362bp favoring AUD. Cross-asset conditions show elevated market volatility with VIX at 22.9, triggering defensive unwinds across high-yielding crosses. Technical structure confirms persistent pressure as AUD/JPY trades at 107.454 while AUD/USD sits in a downtrend below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6951/0.7004/0.7054, extended 4.54 ATR below its 20-day moving average. The combination of scorecard divergence, wide negative carry absorption, and broader risk aversion signals ongoing squeeze risk for AUD/JPY long positions. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; risk-off liquidation overrides substantial carry support. Catalyst: Australia Wage Price Index and Employment Change at 00:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp recovery in broader risk sentiment that restores carry demand and lifts spot above 108.50.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 159.29, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.27/157.52/158.74 as spot consolidates near the 160.00 ceiling. Saxo 1M options show an extreme 25-delta risk reversal of −1.74 alongside an implied volatility of 7.2% against 5.4% 30-day realized volatility, establishing a 1.8-point volatility risk premium. CFTC data for the week ending Nov 10 reflects speculative JPY leveraged funds net short −23,913 contracts at the 90th percentile of its 52-week range, indicating historically crowded short positioning. A 267bp overnight SOFR-TONA spread and Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% rate spread sustain fundamental support, but the pronounced put skew highlights institutional hedging for downside repricing as spot approaches 160.00. 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention concerns. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; topside capped by intervention risk despite solid carry. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes at 19:00 UTC. Risk: Sustained upside break above 160.50 that forces options put-skew liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1011, remaining entirely below its falling SMA20/50/200 moving-average cluster at 1.1164/1.1285/1.1523. CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds heavily net short −98,604 contracts, sitting in the 6th percentile of the 52-week distribution with z = −1.58. Conversely, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows 87% of accounts net long, establishing an acute retail-institutional divergence against the macro downtrend. Policy settings reinforce structural headwinds, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintaining a 135bp rate advantage and a +146bp SOFR-€STR overnight spread favoring USD. FRED data shows US 5Y yields rose +26bp over 5 days driven by real yields (+25bp real vs +1bp breakeven), underscoring US rate support. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; retail long crowding vulnerable to capitulation into technical downtrend. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI report at 10:00 UTC. Risk: Daily close back above the 20-day SMA at 1.1164, relieving downward momentum.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Rates Momentum vs Technical Cluster
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3196, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 moving-average band at 1.3355/1.3334/1.3410. Slower momentum persists on the charts even as 2Y sovereign yield spreads moved +12bp over 5 days and +27bp over 20 days in GBP's favor, reaching +25bp over US 2Y yields. Policy rates are balanced with Fed at 4.00% and BoE at 4.00%, while overnight benchmarks show a mild 8bp carry advantage for the pound with SONIA at 3.98% vs SOFR at 3.90%. CFTC leveraged funds hold net longs of +35,586 contracts (WoW +2,900), indicating steady institutional interest ahead of domestic labor and price figures. The pair remains technically contained below 1.3334 resistance despite firming short-end yield differentials. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; short-end yield resilience checked by overhead trend resistance. Catalyst: UK CPI and Employment reports at 07:00 UTC. Risk: Headline UK CPI print significantly below the 3.7% forecast, eroding short-end yield support.
